title: ～わけではない — “it doesn’t mean ～ / not necessarily”
summary: Partly denies a conclusion that others might draw: “it’s not that ～.” It attaches to the plain form of a verb or adjective (な-adj + な, noun + である/の). Used to avoid a misunderstanding or soften a statement.

patterns.gloss: It is not (necessarily) the case that ～
It’s not even that ～ (adds another denial)

body.p: It does not say “no” to everything. 嫌いなわけではない means “it’s not that I dislike it” — maybe I like it a little, or I just don’t eat it often. It denies the obvious assumption only.
A fact is stated first, then the likely conclusion is denied, then the real situation follows with が or けど: 毎日会っているが、親しいわけではない. The negative form is ～わけではありません in polite speech.
Plain ～ではない states a fact directly. ～わけではない carries “don’t jump to that conclusion”. It is also different from ～わけがない, which means “impossible”.

examples.ja: 嫌（きら）いなわけではないが、あまり食（た）べない。
examples.romaji: Kirai na wake dewa nai ga, amari tabenai.
examples.tr: It’s not that I dislike it, but I don’t eat it much.
examples.note: な-adjective + な + わけではない.

examples.ja: 毎日（まいにち）会（あ）っているが、特別（とくべつ）親（した）しいわけではない。
examples.romaji: Mainichi atte iru ga, tokubetsu shitashii wake dewa nai.
examples.tr: We meet every day, but that doesn’t mean we’re especially close.

examples.ja: 全部（ぜんぶ）が分（わ）からないわけではないが、難（むずか）しい所（ところ）もある。
examples.romaji: Zenbu ga wakaranai wake dewa nai ga, muzukashii tokoro mo aru.
examples.tr: It’s not that I understand nothing, but some parts are difficult.
examples.note: A double negative: not that I don’t understand = I understand some.

pitfalls: It is not a flat “no”. Do not use it to refuse something strongly (that is ～わけにはいかない or ～わけがない).
The な-adjective needs な before わけ: 嫌いなわけではない, not 嫌いわけではない.
